search.label: Kubernetes API Machinery
search.text:
kubernetes api machinery boundedcontext the boundary within which "apply", "manager" and "field" have their
server-side apply meanings.

search.label: Detect and report field conflicts
search.text:
detect and report field conflicts capability reject an apply that changes a field owned by another manager, naming the
manager and the field path.

search.label: Apply an object server-side
search.text: apply an object server-side capability merge an applied configuration into the live object and update managed fields.

search.label: Conflict
search.text:
conflict concept "a conflict occurs when an apply operation tries to change a field that another
manager also claims to manage."

search.label: Field management
search.text:
field management concept "the user relies on and expects the value of the field not to change. the user
who last made an assertion about the value of a field will be recorded as the
current field manager."

search.label: Force
search.text:
force concept setting `force=true` "forces the operation to succeed, changes the value of the
field, and **removes the field from all other managers' entries in
managedfields**."

search.label: last-applied-configuration annotation
search.text:
last-applied-configuration annotation concept the legacy client-side mechanism ssa replaces. tracks a user's last applied
state rather than their field management.

search.label: managedFields
search.text:
managedfields concept an entry in `metadata.managedfields` recording `manager`, `operation`
(`apply` or `update`), `apiversion`, `time`, `fieldstype` (`fieldsv1`) and
`fieldsv1`.

search.label: Ownership transfer
search.text:
ownership transfer concept "whenever a field's value does change, ownership moves from its current manager
to the manager making the change."

search.label: An apply request must name a field manager
search.text:
an apply request must name a field manager invariant **asserted by a test, stated by no fetched document.** the docs describe what a
manager is; the requirement that a request carry one is visible in the test
name.

existing automation or users."

search.label: An entry's timestamp does not update when another manager takes a field over
